sanjay: hey folks — quick sanity check. we're seeing a client edge-case where a service account JWT with an audience `https://api.redwood.internal/` works for normal REST calls but streaming connections fail with 401s. any advices on how OIDC audience/service-account scoping should look in our SDKs?

maya: have you confirmed the aud claim exactly matches the token endpoint we use for websockets? streaming tends to use a different origin in our infra (:thinking:)

sanjay: yeah double-checked. token aud is `https://api.redwood.internal/` and websocket connector uses `wss://stream.redwood.internal/`. REST is fine because we hit the same backend but stream rejects during handshake.

leo: that sounds like expected audience mismatch — websocket layer expects token audience to match `stream.redwood.internal` (no path). Our OIDC doc mentions audience must be the exact principal. do we mint tokens via impersonation or direct SA JWT?

sanjay: we mint by exchanging SA JWT for an access token (impersonation flow) via our token-exchange service. burried in code: `exchangeService.exchange(jwt, scope: 'inference:stream')`

maya: can you paste the exchange call log? maybe the exchange service is normalizing aud to the API origin.

sanjay: pasted logs below:
```
INFO exchange request: subject=svc-account@redwood, requested_aud=https://api.redwood.internal/, scopes=[inference:stream]
INFO exchange response: access_token=ya29..., aud=stream.redwood.internal, expires_in=3600
ERROR stream connect: 401 audience mismatch
```

taylor: hmm the exchange returns aud=stream.redwood.internal but the client verifies aud includes the full URL and fails because it has `https://` prefix. small bug in verifier — it compares exact string.

leo: ah that rings a bell. SDK verifier logic was updated last quarter to allow host-only auds but we missed the websocket verifier path in node and python clients.

maya: good catch. propose: patch websocket auth check to normalize aud (strip scheme + path) and accept host-only tokens OR expect exchange service to return full-url aud consistently. which is less risky?

taylor: safer to relax client verifier to accept both. server-side changes propagate slower (enterprise customers on pinned versions).

sanjay: ok I'm happy with client fix. can someone own a quick PR for node + python? this is affecting a customer integration.

leo: I'll do python. planning to update verifier in `sdk/auth/verifier.py` to: `def normalize_aud(a): return urlparse(a).netloc` then compare against `expected_host`. i'll add unit tests.

taylor: i'll take node. PR will be small: switch from `aud === expected` to `normalizeAndCompare(aud, expected)` and add streaming test harness. linking ticket: https://go/issue/INF-8923

maya: add a changelog entry and a note in the SDK migration guide about aud normalization. also add one e2e where exchange returns `stream.redwood.internal` and client accepts `https://stream.redwood.internal/`

devex-bot: Reminder: create PRs against `release/v0.12.x` for patch backports and tag @devex-oncall when merging. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks all. pinging for code review: leo -> PR 548 on python, taylor -> PR 1123 on node. can we aim to ship hotfix today? customer needs workaround by EOD.

leo: PR 548 opened, request review from @maya and @taylor. cc @sanjay.

taylor: PR 1123 opened. added e2e script and local repro steps in the PR description. will try to get reviews in the next 2 hours.

maya: reviewing now. if both green i'll trigger canary and tag infra for a quick rollout.

sanjay: awesome. if anything blocks, ping here and i'll take over manual test steps. :rocket:
